opening.spoken: This record covers the claimed solution of Erdős problem #1133: what has been claimed, what it rests on, and what would have to be checked by whom.

short_version.spoken: Erdős conjectured that for any large set of nodes in [-1,1] one can choose bounded target values so that any polynomial of slightly higher degree matching most of them must be large somewhere on the interval. In September 2026 Jia-Qi Yang listed a claimed proof with stronger quantitative results, as a PDF in a public repository. There is no Lean development, so nothing here can be settled by a rerun. Everything here is open.

background.spoken: Fix a bound C. The conjecture is that there is a small epsilon such that, for n large and any n nodes in [-1,1], one can pick target values in [-1,1] so that every polynomial of degree below (1 + epsilon) n which hits at least (1 - epsilon) n of the targets exceeds C in absolute value somewhere on [-1,1]. Erdős proved a related statement with the roles of degree and node count exchanged and said he could not prove the conjectured one even when the counts are equal.

background.spoken: The claim proves the conjectured statement and more: the obstruction holds for sign data with any prescribed pointwise tolerance below one, the optimal exponential order of the obstruction parameter is determined, and for the full Chebyshev–Lobatto grids a sharp leading exponential coefficient is identified. The author cites a quantitative interpolation estimate of Olevskii and Ulanovskii for the arbitrary-node case, and describes the submission as a quantitative refinement of an earlier draft.
